cards.body:
*Lesson 6.3 · Portfolio & Templates*

_≈ 2 hours · with Miracle_

Nobody hires a builder they can't see. You've built more than thirty working systems in this course, and the proof-of-work logs to show it. Now turn the best of them into a portfolio that wins calls: short case studies with real numbers, three-minute demos, and clean, documented templates someone else can import and run, without your secrets or your customers' data hiding inside.

*Your problem:* Clients want proof before they pay you.
*The plan:* Build a case study, a demo and a sellable template, safely cleaned of secrets.
*After this lesson:* You have a portfolio that wins work.

*"Show me something you've built"*

*The call:* A school administrator asks for examples. Tolu scrolls through 40 workflow screenshots, explaining each one. The call goes quiet.

*The problem:* Clients don't buy nodes. They buy "your orders are confirmed in seconds, and you got your evenings back".

*Tolu's fix:* Three stories, each one page and three minutes of video: the problem, what she built, and the numbers afterwards.

*Glitch:* "Share the template! It's only a JSON file. Nobody reads JSON." (Attackers do.)
*The one-page case study*
Code example on screen (The one-page case study): open it in the app.
Hands-on lab: The one-page case study. It's interactive, so open it in the app and try it there.

*Tolu:* Your proof-of-work logs already hold most of this. Course projects count too, labelled honestly as "built for a fictional business, Harvest Lane, with test data". Never invent a client or inflate a number. One true number beats five impressive guesses.

*The three-minute demo*

_Time · Show_
- *0:00–0:30* · The problem, from the customer's side ("Iya Basira sends an order at 9 p.m. and waits until morning")
- *0:30–1:45* · The solution working, from the customer's side: the phone, the reply, the confirmation
- *1:45–2:30* · Behind the scenes, briefly: the workflow, one safety feature (approval, error alert)
- *2:30–3:00* · The result in numbers, and one sentence on who this suits

Use test data and test accounts on screen. Zoom in on what matters; hide your email, tokens and other tabs. Record twice; send the better one.

*What a shareable template needs*

- *No secrets*: Platforms don't export credential secrets, but anything you typed into a field (a header token, a key in a URL) goes along.
- *No personal data*: Pinned test data travels inside an n8n workflow file. So do hard-coded emails, phone numbers and chat IDs.
- *No hidden dependencies*: Sheet IDs, sub-workflow IDs and webhook paths point at _your_ accounts. Replace them with placeholders and explain them in the README.
- *Sticky notes*: Short notes on the canvas: what each section does, what to change.
- *Tested on a fresh account*: Import it into a clean n8n (or a new Make or Zapier account) and set it up from the README alone. Whatever you had to guess, add to the README.

Each platform shares differently: n8n exports workflow JSON; Make exports a scenario blueprint; Zapier lets you share a copy of a Zap. The same rules apply to all three.

*Try it: clean a workflow before sharing*

Paste an exported n8n workflow (or use Glitch's sample). The checker finds common secrets and personal data, removes pinned data and shows a cleaned copy. Everything stays in your browser.
Hands-on lab: Try it: clean a workflow before sharing. It's interactive, so open it in the app and try it there.
*The README*
Code example on screen (The README): open it in the app.
Hands-on lab: The README. It's interactive, so open it in the app and try it there.

cards.body:
*Solved problem: Boss 3 as a sellable template*

*The goal.* Turn the Telegram order bot into a package another business can buy and set up in 15 minutes: a clean workflow file, a sample sheet, a README, a setup video and a case study.

*Step 1 · Generalise it*

Duplicate the workflow. Rename "Harvest Lane" things to neutral names ("Your shop"). Move business settings (delivery fee, free-delivery threshold, 50-unit limit, Tolu's chat ID) into one *Edit Fields · Settings* node at the start, so buyers change them in one place. Add sticky notes for each section.

*Step 2 · Clean it*

Unpin all data. Move any typed-in key into a credential. Export, run the file through Card 4, and fix anything found at the source (not just in the file). Replace the sheet ID with `<YOUR_SHEET_ID>`. Read the final JSON once yourself.

*Step 3 · Make a sample sheet*

A Google Sheet with the Price_List, Customers, Pending and Orders tabs, ten fake products and two fake customers, shared as "anyone with the link can make a copy" (view-only for the original).

*Step 4 · Test on a fresh account*

Create a new n8n Cloud trial (or a fresh Docker volume), a new Telegram test bot and a copy of the sheet. Follow only the README. Time it. Each time you had to look something up, fix the README. Target: under 15 minutes.

*Step 5 · Write the case study and record the demo*

From your Boss 3 log: problem (Tolu pricing orders by hand at night), build (bot, pricing from the sheet, confirm buttons, daily report), safety (prices never from AI; big orders to a human), results (your test numbers, labelled as test results). Record the three-minute demo following Card 2.

- *15 min* setup on a fresh account, from the README alone
- *0* secrets, phone numbers or pinned records in the file
- *5* pieces: workflow, sheet, README, video, case study

*Nodo's tip:* put each template in its own GitHub repository (or folder) with the workflow file, README and changelog. When n8n changes something, you update once and every buyer gets the fix.

*Why this approach works*

- Clients see outcomes and numbers, not node diagrams.
- Settings in one node make the template easy to adapt.
- Cleaning at the source stops secrets returning in the next export.
- A fresh-account test proves the README actually works.
- Honest labels ("test data") build trust.

*Common mistakes to avoid*

- Screenshots of nodes as a portfolio.
- Sharing exports with pinned customer data.
- Keys typed into header fields.
- READMEs written from memory, never tested.
- Invented clients or numbers.

*Glitch hunt*

*Glitch:* I helped publish your templates. Five surprises.

*A:* A buyer imports the template and every request fails: it's calling your Paystack account with your key.
*B:* A buyer emails: "Who is Funmi, and why is her order in my workflow?"
*C:* The buyer's import errors: "Google Sheet not found".
*D:* Three buyers asked the same setup question in the first week.
*E:* A prospect asks to speak to the "pharmacy client" in your case study. There isn't one.

cards.prompt: Made your call on each one? Tap Reveal to check.
cards.answer:
*A:* a key typed into a header field travelled with the export. Revoke that key now, move it into a credential, re-export, and tell buyers which credential to create.
*B:* pinned test data with personal details shipped in the file. Unpin before export, and check with Card 4.
*C:* a hard-coded sheet ID pointing at your sheet. Use a placeholder and a copyable sample sheet, explained in the README.
*D:* the README wasn't tested on a fresh account. Add the answer, and test again.
*E:* an invented client. Remove it. Use real clients (with permission) or clearly labelled course projects.

cards.title: Bronze (+25 XP): One case study
cards.body:
- Pick your strongest Boss Battle and write its one-page case study from your proof-of-work log.
- Every number must come from your log, labelled "test results" where they are.

*Done when:*
- A non-technical friend can tell you, after one read, what problem it solves and what changed, with a number.

cards.title: Silver (+50 XP): A three-minute demo and a clean template
cards.body:
- Record a three-minute demo of the same project using the Card 2 structure.
- Package its workflow as a template: settings node, sticky notes, cleaned export, README and sample sheet.
- Have someone else set it up from the README on a fresh account.

*Done when:*
- They succeed in under 20 minutes without asking you, and Card 4 finds nothing in the file.

cards.title: Gold (+100 XP): Your portfolio page
cards.body:
- Publish a portfolio page with three projects (case study, demo video and, where suitable, a template link), a short "who I help" line, your offer tiers from 6.2, and a booking link.
- Send it to three people in your target market and ask one question: "What would make you book a call?"

*Done when:*
- The page is live, three people have seen it, and you've changed it based on their answers.

cards.q: What should a case study lead with?
cards.why: Clients buy outcomes: “orders confirmed in 30 seconds” beats a diagram.

cards.q: Which of these travels inside an exported n8n workflow file?
options: Pinned data and anything typed into fields
cards.why: Credential secrets stay behind; pinned data and typed-in values go along.

cards.q: A key was typed into a header and shared in a template. First step?
options: Revoke the key immediately, then fix the template
Ask buyers not to use it
cards.why: Assume it's compromised: revoke, replace, then clean the source.

cards.q: How do you know your README works?
options: Someone sets the template up on a fresh account using only the README
cards.why: Test documentation like you test workflows.

cards.q: You only have course projects. How do you present them?
options: As real clients, to look experienced
Honestly, as projects for a fictional business with test data, with real test numbers
cards.why: Honesty builds trust; real test numbers still show what you can do.

cards.body:
*Remember this*

1. Show outcomes: problem → build → result, with honest numbers.
2. Three minutes of demo, customer's view first.
3. Templates carry what you typed and pinned. Clean at the source.
4. Settings in one node, sticky notes, placeholders, a sample sheet.
5. Test the README on a fresh account.
6. Never invent clients; label course work clearly.

*Lesson 6.3 complete!* _Portfolio & Templates_ is done and saved to your progress, on WhatsApp and in the app.

Next up: Capstone 6.4, _Grand Capstone: Harvest Lane on Autopilot_.
